title: From love (10:1)
hookLine: serving for reward or from fear is not the highest way
tomorrow: what does someone acting from love do when nobody's watching?

cards: Ask a room why they do the right thing, and the honest answers often come in two kinds. Because it pays off. Or because something bad happens if you don't: grades, bosses, a speed camera.

Maimonides opens the last chapter of his laws of return by naming both and setting them aside. Let no one say, he writes, I'll keep the commandments to get the blessings, or stay away from wrongs so I won't be cursed.
Serving that way, he says, is serving from fear.

teach.h: NOT FOR REWARD, NOT FROM FEAR.
teach.b: It isn't worthless, he says; beginners are taught to start there.

teach.h: THE WAY OF PROPHETS AND SAGES.
teach.b: But it isn't the way of the prophets or the sages. Their way is from love. Tomorrow opens what that looks like.

teach.h: A WEEK OF RETURN, LOOKED BACK ON.
teach.b: Today, the week ends, and it's worth looking back down the road. Traits need turning: the anger and envy under the act. Beloved, not far, standing where the spotless can't.
Yesterday far, today close, and two sages arguing about who's greeted first. Let them be new: no reminding, not even as a joke. No body, only closeness: the world to come as nearness.
Blessings are tools: the rain clears time. Set them side by side, and they've been walking toward this word all week. Why turn a temper nobody else sees?
Why welcome a returner first? Why hold back the funny line about someone's past, or use a gift for more than yourself? Not for the prize, and not from fear.

how: Jewish teachers often cite Antigonus in Pirkei Avot, be like servants who serve without thought of reward, and Maimonides' chapter ten is studied as the high point of his laws of return.

o: serving God out of a strong sense of duty
serving God for the blessings promised to you
serving God for no reward and out of no fear

games.q: the week's ways to serve — tap the pairs.
p: serving from fear, by his count
the way of prophets and sages

s: Maimonides says serving for a reward is worthless
beginners are taught to start there. it just isn't the highest way.
for Maimonides, serving to get blessings counts as serving from fear
the one who serves for blessings or against curses serves from fear.
this week's laws were about deeds alone
traits, the words we say about others, even how we use gifts: all of it.

games.q: you find a wallet on the bus and return it. which reason is Maimonides' 'from love'?
o: so good things come back to you someday.
so you won't feel guilty about it later.
because it's theirs, and that's enough.
games.why: the first is reward, the second is fear, and Maimonides counts both as serving from fear. the third is the road toward love.

practice: Choose one small thing you'll do in the next hour anyway: rinse a cup, answer a message, hold a door. Decide now to do it for no reward and from no fear, simply because it's good. Then rest with that one choice until the bell.

wordCard.voice: From love: Maimonides' name for the highest way to serve, not for reward and not out of fear.

orig.note: Hebrew: from love, Maimonides' phrase for the highest service.

carryVoice: To carry: from love, where this week's six lines were heading. End of the week, twenty-four of thirty.

sources.ref: Mishneh Torah, Laws of Return (Hilkhot Teshuvah) 10:1 (don't serve to receive blessings or avoid curses; that is serving from fear, not the level of prophets or sages; beginners are taught that way until they serve from love)
Mishnah Avot 1:3 (Antigonus of Sokho: don't be like servants who serve for a reward)
